promise: We will deliver the NHS 18-week waiting-time guarantee by 2029
description: Announced on the NHS's 77th anniversary that the government would restore the constitutional right to be treated within 18 weeks by 2029. NHS waiting lists remained above 7 million through 2025, so the guarantee is a long way off but formally remains the government's target.
evidence: Announcement made July 13, 2025 alongside the NHS Constitution
Backlog remained ~7.5 million patients as of 2025

promise: 8% annual economic growth by the end of his term (2029)
description: Growth was 5.0% (2024) and ~5.1% (2025), with IMF forecasts of ~4.9–5.1% through 2029 — far below the 8% target.

promise: Deliver 1.5 million new homes over the parliament via radical planning reform
description: The planning reform was delivered — Planning and Infrastructure Act received royal assent 18 Dec 2025 — but housing delivery has not come close to the required pace, and the 1.5m target is widely regarded as at risk.

promise: Achieve 8% economic growth by 2029, after 5.8-6.5% growth in 2027
description: Presenting the macroeconomic framework to Parliament in May 2026, President Prabowo said he was confident Indonesia's economy could grow between 5.8% and 6.5% in 2027, heading toward 8% growth by 2029. Analysts warned the 8% target would be hard to reach after Q2 2026 growth slowed.
evidence: 8% growth by 2029 restated in the May 2026 macroeconomic framework
Q2 2026 growth slowed, with experts doubting the trajectory

promise: India will become the world's third-largest economy by 2029 (end of his third term)
description: Modi guaranteed India would become the world's third-largest economy by the end of his third term in 2029. As of mid-2026, analysts said the targets were off track, with projections for India overtaking Germany and Japan slipping toward 2028-2030.
evidence: Third-largest economy pledge tied to the end of Modi's third term (2029)
2026 analysis said the target was off track; Morgan Stanley projected 2028

promise: Pledge €700 million to the Global Fund's eighth replenishment (2026-2029) to fight HIV, tuberculosis and malaria
description: At the One Health Summit on April 7, 2026, the European Commission announced its intention to pledge €700 million overall for the Global Fund's eighth replenishment, with €185 million immediately available under the current long-term budget. Country-level grants under the replenishment are to be implemented from 2027 to 2029, and the pledge remains subject to the outcome of the Multiannual Financial Framework negotiations.
evidence: Commission announced the €700 million pledge intention on April 7, 2026
Grants under the eighth replenishment to be implemented 2027-2029
